PG 17 docs: "LIMIT and OFFSET allow you to retrieve just a portion of the rows that are generated by the rest of the query"; "OFFSET says to skip that many rows before beginning to return rows." Lab curl ?maxPriceVnd=500000&limit=2&offset=1 → [{"id":5,...},{"id":8,...}]; logged SQL has WHERE before ORDER BY/LIMIT/OFFSET.

Opinion with a condition ("when the result is still the same resource"). Both supporting facts now hold for this code: a per-filter action would have to redeclare [FromQuery] limit/offset and repeat OrderBy/Skip/Take (ProductsController.List lines 23-45), and a fixed route like /products/cheap carries one condition, so combining needs another endpoint or a query parameter. The round-1 overstatement ("cheap" plus a page needs another endpoint) is gone from s6 and quiz q1 b.

Follows from PG 17 docs: OFFSET/LIMIT apply to "the rows that are generated by the rest of the query"; if the price condition is not in the SQL, those rows include non-matching products, so offset counts them and a later C# filter leaves fewer than `limit`. Loading every row to filter in C# reads the whole table by construction (stage-1 List() had no Where).
